energy-momentum-relation.title: On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies
energy-momentum-relation.abstract: The relativistic energy-momentum relation E^2 = (pc)^2 + (mc^2)^2 is derived from the principles of special relativity, relating invariant mass, momentum, and energy.

variable-mass.title: Dynamics of systems with variable mass
variable-mass.abstract: The Meshchersky equation describes the motion of variable mass systems. It accounts for momentum transfer during accretion and ejection, modifying Newton's second law for rockets and jet propulsion.

weak-form-newton.title: Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics
weak-form-newton.abstract: Newton's third law in its weak form states that the internal action and reaction forces between particles in an isolated system are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, which guarantees conservation of linear momentum.

strong-form-newton.title: Classical Mechanics
strong-form-newton.abstract: The strong form of Newton's third law requires that forces between two particles are not only equal and opposite but also collinear, acting along the line connecting their centers, ensuring angular momentum conservation.
